02.12.2004
Hon'ble Rajesh Tandon, J.
Heard Sri Arvind Vashisth, counsel for the petitioner and
Standing counsel for the respondents.
By the present writ petition, the petitioners have prayed
for a writ of certiorari quashing the order dated 25.05.2004 passed
by the Additional District Judge/F.T.C.-Vth, Dehradun
in Misc. Appeal No. 28 of 2004 (Raj Kumar Vs. Murti Sri
Raghunathjee Maharaj and others)

Briefly stated, the facts giving rise to the present writ
petition are that the petitioners filed a Suit in the court of Civil
Judge (Sr. Div.), Dehradun against the defendant for
permanent injunction restraining the defendant not to interfere
in possession of the plaintiff over the property in suit.
The plaintiff alleged that it is a charitable society and
looks-after the property of Murti Sri Raghunathjee Maharaj.
The temple of Sri Raghunathjee Maharaj is 200 years old. The
property of the temple consists of Dharam Shala and Charitable
Hospital and a piece of land measuring 1,200 sq.metre yard and
houses etc. In order to arrange free stay of devotees, the
management took a decision to construct four rooms at the first
floor Ghat Road. For this purpose, a map was prepared and
presented for sanction before the municipal authorities. The
plaintiff alleged that respondent no. 5 with the help of
respondent no. 2 to 4 stopped the construction of the rooms
while work was going on for putting a linter.
The plaintiff ahs further alleged that respondent no. 5 has
annoyance with the management of the Society as his father,
who is now 80 years of age was Pujari in the temple, he was
replaced by another Pujari, which infuriated him and
respondent no. 6.
The petitioner has submitted that in order to caused undue
damage to the plaintiffs/petitioners the respondent no. 5 in
active connivance with respondent no. 2 to 4 stopped
construction of the room and under these circumstances
plaintiffs/petitioners were constrained to institute a suit in the
Court of Civil Judge (Sr. Div.), Dehradun with a prayer of
perpetual injunction restraining Defendants (Respondent NO. 2
to 5) from interfering in the management of property of the

temple and from raising any new construction. The suit was
numbered as O.S. NO. 54/2004.
On 29.01.2004, the Civil Judge (Senior Division)
Dehradun has considered the urgency of the situation, and has
passed an order dispensing the notices under Section 80 C.P.C
to the defendants.
It is alleged that on an application for interim injunction,
the court issued notices to the defendant and fixed 06.02.2004.
On 09.03.2004, the court below has allowed the
application for interim injunction ex-parte and restrained the
defendants accordingly.
The respondent no. 6 has moved an application under
Order 1 Rule 10 of C.P.C. on 24.03.2004, which is still pending
for disposal.
During the pendency of the application under Order 1
Rule 10 C.P.C., respondent no. 6 has presented the aforesaid
appeal before the respondent no. 1.
Aggrieved by the order dated 09.03.2004, the respondent
no. 6 has preferred and appeal being Misc. Appeal No. 26 of
2004. While admitting the appeal, the appellate court has
directed the parties to maintain status quo.
Counsel for the petitioner has stated that respondent no.
6 has failed to disclose his grievance, hence he has no locus
standi to present the appeal.
A Perusal of the order dated 25.05.2004 passed by the
appellate court shows that the petitioners were permitted to
remove shuttering from the linter in order to avoid any loss to
them. The appellate court also directed the trial court to
pass appropriate order on the application of the defendant
under Order 1 Rule 10 C.P.C.

I find no reason to interfere with the order passed by the
appellate court. However, the trial court is directed to decide
the suit within a period of three months. For a period of three
months alone parties are directed to maintain status quo.
Any observation made above will not affect either the
decision of the case before the trial court or the decision on the
application under Order 1 Rule 10 C.P.C. on merits.
Subject to the aforesaid observation, writ petition is
disposed of. No order as to costs.
02.12.2004 (RAJESH TANDON, J.)
